title: Multi-endpoint Harmonization PRD and Launch Checklist (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD for harmonizing and launching the hosted API surface for text generation (chat/completions), embeddings, and rerank. This ticket consolidates requirements, documents scope changes since initial draft, and provides a prescriptive acceptance and launch checklist to align product, engineering, and DX. Goal: ship a consistent, observable, and backward-compatible hosted API set with predictable performance and clear fallbacks for production customers.
background: We currently maintain separate hosted routes for chat, completions, embeddings, and a standalone rerank endpoint. Customers request unified contracts, consistent streaming and structured output behavior, and clearer downgrade paths when capacity or model variants are used. This work harmonizes behavior and launches a coordinated docs + SDK + console rollout.
goals: Define definitive API contracts and examples for each endpoint family
Ship backend and SDK changes with backward-compatible defaults
Deliver monitoring, billing, and runbooks required for SLA-grade production usage
Enable automated rollout (canary -> regional -> global) with safe rollback
out_of_scope: On-prem private deployment packaging (handled by Private team in separate epic)
New model training or model onboarding (model catalog team owns this)
Large-scale re-architecture of runtime sharding beyond targeted kernel optimizations
scope_changes: ADDED: Structured 'metadata' field for embeddings responses to include vector_version and source_model
CHANGED: Streaming contract for chat will include per-token provenance tags (opt-in) instead of mandatory in v1
REMOVED: Experimental 'batch_rerank' public flag; replaced with an internal-only beta behind feature flag
DEFERRED: Support for 2048->32768 token auto-scaling and corresponding billing change (post-launch)
CLARIFICATION: 'completions' route remains available as alias of 'generate' for backward compatibility; new SDKs will prefer 'generate'
requirements: API: OpenAPI spec and one-page contract for chat, generate (completions), embeddings, and rerank routes
Backward compatibility: Existing keys and request fields must continue to work without breaking changes
Streaming: Chat/generate support chunked streaming over HTTP and websocket fallback for legacy clients
Embeddings: deterministic vector size validation and documented normalization behavior
Rerank: stable scoring contract (0..1) and deterministic tie-breaking rules
Auth & Quotas: per-key rate limiting and usage tags for cost breakdowns in console
SDKs: JavaScript/Go/Python SDKs released with examples and migration notes
Telemetry: tracing, per-route token breakdowns, latency p95/p99, error-rate dashboards
SLOs: latency SLOs defined by model class and region (see metrics)
Canary: ability to route X% traffic to new contract variants and automatic fallback on error spike
acceptance_criteria: Documentation: OpenAPI published, examples for each endpoint (chat, generate, embeddings, rerank) and migration guide published to docs.redwood.ai
SDKs: NPM, PyPI, and Go module published and smoke-tested by solutions-engineering
Compatibility: 100% of samples from existing SDK test-suite must produce same shape responses unless opt-in fields are enabled
Performance: single-request median latency under 120ms for short chat tokens (<= 128) on hosted tier; p99 under 800ms
Throughput: endpoints sustain target throughput on dedicated canary cluster (see ENG-1984 load plan)
Stability: error rate <= 0.5% during 24-hour canary at target load otherwise rollback triggers
Observability: dashboards with token-level cost and latency, per-route tracers, and alerting configured in Console
Billing: per-token billing unit validated in staging with billing-service and invoices sample generated
Security: KMS-integrations tested for customer key scenarios; security review completed
Support readiness: runbook published, support playbook and escalation contacts documented, support team trained
launch_checklist: Finalize and lock OpenAPI spec + sample requests/responses
Merge SDK PRs and tag releases (JS/Python/Go)
Publish docs + migration guide and update quickstart templates
Enable canary routing plumbing and configure 1% -> 10% -> 50% gradual rollout plan
Execute 24-hour canary with synthetic load and customer-like workloads
Validate billing and cost dashboards with real token accounting
Run automated regression evals against canonical prompt set (quality gates pass)
Console: add per-route toggles for streaming, function-calling and model variant fallbacks
Create internal incident runbook and Slack/ops channels; schedule support Q&A
Prepare customer outbound comms (beta cohort and general availability launch emails)
Tag release in deployment orchestration and coordinate cross-team deploy window
Security sign-off and compliance checklist complete
Create rollback playbook and automated revert trigger thresholds
metrics: Tokens served per minute by route
Cost per 1K tokens by route and model variant
Error rate and distribution by HTTP status and internal error code
Canary health signals: CPU/GPU utilization, tail latency, queue depth
Quality regressions: automated eval score delta vs baseline
risks_mitigation: Risk: Unexpected quality regressions from model variant fallbacks -> Mitigation: gate fallbacks behind quality checks and rollback on eval delta > threshold
Risk: Billing mismatch due to different tokenization in embeddings -> Mitigation: add tokenization shim in staging and reconcile with billing(fx) team
Risk: Streaming contract causes client SDK breakage -> Mitigation: maintain old non-streaming path and offer opt-in streaming in SDKs
Risk: Canaries generate noisy alerts -> Mitigation: tune alert thresholds for canary window and require correlation across signals before paging
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal beta (1% traffic) with SDKs and partners. Phase 2: customer beta (10%) with opt-in customers and monitoring. Phase 3: regional ramp to 50% and then global GA after 72h stable. Automatic rollback thresholds configured at error-rate and latency deltas.
stakeholders: Eng leads: Miguel Ortega, Sara Kline
notes: Design decision: kept 'rerank' as a separate logical endpoint due to differing request/response shapes despite common internal scoring pipeline
Ask from sales: add a quick 'latency guarantee' blurb for enterprise SKUs in console — requires legal review
Follow-up: evaluate merged 'generate' alias deprecation timeline post-GA (6 months target)
